Commentary.Commentary: The visitors were brilliant for most parts! Andy McBrine and Barry McCarthy were absolutely brilliant and took their side on top but they have let the advantage slip away big time due to the last wicket stand. They'll now have to bat really well, their first aim will be to get past the new ball without much damage. Zimbabwe on the other hand, would want early wickets and put the Irish under pressure.

Ireland didn't take long to get the last wicket in this session but Zimbabwe have managed to take the lead! Remarkable effort, they were down and out at one stage. Except for Welch, wickets kept falling. He held fort at one end but kept losing partners. When he fell, his side still trailed by over 50, the last pair though batted brilliantly and have taken their side into the lead.

Commentary.Commentary: We're all set for the action to begin! The players make their way out to the middle.

An outstanding spell by Blessing Muzarabani had the Irish in massive trouble earlier on. The lower order though came to the fore for the visitors as Andy McBrine and Mark Adair put up over 100 to take them to an decent score. Zimbabwe however in reply, have began well. Still though they trail by below 200 but are in a strong position to take the lead. Ireland on the other hand, will hope for some early wickets to put the pressure back onto the hosts. An important first session awaits.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

Ireland though replied brilliantly with Mark Adair, Andy McBrine and Lorcan Tucker. It was the stand between Tucker and McBrine that steadied the ship, once the former fell, Adair came in and played with the same intensity to get back into the game. The duo added more than 120 runs and got the score above 200 however, it was Andy McBrine's unbeaten 90 which helped Ireland to get over 260 which looked impossible at one stage. In reply, Zimbabwe lost Ben Curran but Kaitano and Welch looked well settled after that. They'll hope to start Day 2 similarly but Ireland will hope for a much improved performance with the ball. Join us for the action at 8 am GMT and earlier for the build up. Till then, cheers!

So, Zimbabwe end Day 1 on top. They'll be really happy with the position they are in. Zimbabwe were asked to bowl first and their pace attack made amends straightaway. The tall, right arm pacer, Blessing Muzarabani was at his best today as he ended with superb figures of 7/58. He rattled through the top order and put Ireland on the back foot. His short deliveries were unplayable and trouble the opposition dearly.
